summary.text: Currently completing a Bachelor of Honours in Computer Science at the University of Pretoria, building on my BSc IT from NWU with a deep focus on artificial intelligence, machine learning and research methodology. The programme requires a minimum of 120 credits of postgraduate coursework and culminates in an independent research dissertation supervised by a faculty member. Admission requires a 60% average over all third-year Computer Science modules.

items.title: Research Methodology & Project
items.text: A two-part compulsory module. The first semester covers research best practices: designing rigorous studies, conducting literature reviews and structuring academic writing. The project component then applies these methods to produce an original technical research report — which can be a new piece of software, a model, an algorithm, or a theoretical contribution — in one of the department's active research areas.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence I
items.subtitle: Genetic Programming & Grammatical Evolution
items.text: Focuses on Evolutionary Computation and Swarm Intelligence as two Computational Intelligence paradigms. Covers genetic algorithms, genetic programming, grammatical evolution, evolutionary strategies, differential evolution and co-evolution — all modelling Darwinian evolution. Also explores swarm-based optimisers such as ant colony optimisation and particle swarm optimisation, applied to multi-objective and dynamic complex problem spaces.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence II
items.subtitle: Neural Networks
items.text: Covers three Computational Intelligence paradigms. Artificial Neural Networks are studied in depth — including supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning, and the factors that govern network performance. Artificial Immune Systems model the human biological immune system (negative selection, clonal selection, network and danger theory). Fuzzy Systems introduce reasoning under uncertainty using fuzzy logic and rough sets.

items.title: Software Engineering I
items.text: A comprehensive study of contemporary software engineering theory and practice, addressing the challenges of scale, complexity and urgency in real-world systems. Covers design, development, deployment and ongoing operation of software, and shows how standardisation and reuse strategies lead to software that is predictable, repeatable, robust and aligned with user requirements.

items.title: Data Mining
items.text: Covers the full knowledge-discovery pipeline from raw data to actionable insight. Topics include process models (CRISP-DM and SEMMA), exploratory data analysis, dimensionality reduction via PCA and feature selection, descriptive modelling (clustering and association rules), and predictive modelling using decision trees, k-NN, Naive Bayes, neural networks and ensemble methods. Text and image mining are also introduced.

items.title: Natural Language Processing
items.text: Introduces students to data and information analytics through mining both structured and unstructured text data. Students apply generative AI techniques to extract insights from data and use novel methods to collect and analyse personal and public web postings through big data case studies. The module develops knowledge of core NLP algorithms — covering information extraction, machine translation, text summarisation and question answering — and the underlying algorithmic and linguistic foundations needed to work with real-world textual data.

items.title: Image Processing
items.text: A special-topics module in which the Department of Computer Science presents current and advanced research themes. In the current year the topic is digital image processing: covering the mathematical and algorithmic foundations of acquiring, transforming and analysing images. Topics include spatial-domain and frequency-domain filtering (Fourier transforms), edge detection, morphological operations, image segmentation and feature extraction — the core building blocks for computer vision systems applied in fields from medical imaging to autonomous vehicles.

research.title: Research Focus
research.heading: Dissertation — How good are LLMs in providing formative feedback and automated scoring for Regular Expression pedagogy.
text: Teaching tools that check students' regular expression answers can tell them if they're wrong, but not why — and that explanation gap is where learning breaks down. This research investigates whether large language models (GPT-4o and Gemini) can fill that gap by generating accurate scores and genuinely useful, natural-language feedback on student submissions. The study tests three prompting strategies — zero-shot, few-shot, and chain-of-thought — to identify which approach produces the most reliable grading and the most actionable feedback, giving educators concrete guidance on how to actually deploy these tools in a classroom.

summary.text: Completed my BSc in Information Technology at NWU Potchefstroom, where the degree's focus on programming fundamentals and methodology gave me practical experience across a wide range of languages and paradigms. Java formed the backbone of object-oriented programming; C#, JavaScript, HTML and SQL were used for GUIs, webpages and database systems; Python for a chat-app architecture and data analysis projects; and MATLAB and R for mathematics, physics and statistics modules. I took a leading role in team projects, applying Agile methodology across the full software development lifecycle.

items.title: Advanced Databases
items.text: Extended topics covering database optimisation, transactions, indexing strategies, distributed databases and big-data storage patterns.

items.title: Decision Support Systems I

items.title: Decision Support Systems II
items.text: Advanced DSS topics including model-driven and data-driven decision systems, dashboards and predictive analytics pipelines.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence
items.text: Foundations of AI including search algorithms, knowledge representation, machine learning concepts and practical applications.

items.title: Computer Networks
items.text: TCP/IP protocol suite, network architectures, routing, switching, network services administration and troubleshooting.

items.title: Operating Systems
items.text: Process management, memory management, file systems, concurrency and the principles underlying modern OS design.

items.title: IT Developments
items.text: Current and emerging trends in the IT industry, covering topics such as cloud computing, IoT, cyber security and the future of software.

items.label: Object-Oriented
items.text: Java was the primary language for object-oriented programming — covering inheritance, polymorphism, design patterns and data structures. C# was used for GUI development and Windows application projects.

items.label: Web & Databases
items.text: HTML, CSS and JavaScript were used to build interactive webpages and front-end interfaces. SQL drove all database work — from schema design through to stored procedures and complex joins.

items.label: Data & Analysis
items.text: Python was used for building a chat-app back-end architecture as well as data analysis and scripting tasks. R and MATLAB covered statistical computing, mathematical modelling and physics simulations.
